fact: A calf is a young cow.
A foal is a young horse.
A piglet is a young pig.
A lamb is a young sheep.
A kid is a young goat.
A chick is a young chicken.
A duckling is a young duck.
A gosling is a young goose.
A baby rabbit is often called a bunny or kit.
A kitten is a young cat.
A puppy is a young dog.
A fawn is a young deer.
Lion cubs are born with spotted coats that fade as they grow.
Tiger cubs stay with their mother while they learn to hunt.
Bear cubs are born very small compared with adult bears.
Elephant calves use their trunks more skillfully as they grow.
Giraffe calves can stand and walk soon after birth.
Zebra foals can recognize their mothers by stripe patterns and scent.
Rhino calves stay close to their mothers for protection.
Hippo calves can nurse underwater.
A baby kangaroo is called a joey.
Koala joeys spend months developing inside their mother's pouch.
Wallaby joeys also grow in a pouch.
Wombat joeys live in a backward-facing pouch.
Penguin chicks are covered in soft down feathers.
Baby owls are called owlets.
A young eagle is called an eaglet.
Flamingo chicks are born with gray or white down.
A baby puffin is called a puffling.
Young seals are called pups.
Sea lion pups can recognize their mothers by calls.
Dolphin calves swim beside their mothers from birth.
Whale calves drink rich milk from their mothers.
Orca calves stay with family groups called pods.
Many young sharks are called pups.
Sea turtle hatchlings crawl toward the ocean after leaving the nest.
Crocodile mothers may help hatchlings reach the water.
Young alligators often stay near their mother.
Some baby snakes hatch from eggs ready to move on their own.
Many young lizards look like tiny versions of adults.
A froglet is a young frog that has recently grown legs.
Tadpoles are the aquatic young of frogs and toads.
Young axolotls keep feathery external gills.
Baby monkeys cling to their mothers for safety.
Gorilla infants ride on their mothers as they grow.
Young chimpanzees learn by watching older group members.
Orangutan young stay with their mothers for many years.
Baby meerkats are called pups.
Otter pups learn to swim as they grow.
A young fox is called a kit or cub.
Wolf pups are raised by members of the pack.
Coyote pups are born in sheltered dens.
Young raccoons often stay with their mother for many months.
A baby hedgehog is called a hoglet.
Baby squirrels are born hairless and helpless.
A baby bat is called a pup.
A baby porcupine is called a porcupette.
A baby llama is called a cria.
A baby alpaca is also called a cria.
Camel calves can stand and walk not long after birth.
